meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Conclusive. A machine's guess, and the people who sell these tools say in print not to punish a student on the score alone. What else do you have, Hale?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now the essay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend, Hale, and kids paste a finished draft into the file they hand in.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn it closer. A seventeen-year-old who misremembers a line has made a mistake, not used a machine, and he told me he doesn't even know how. Where did that line come from, then?
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale. That's what an outline is for. And you still haven't told me where that line came from.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class, sprung on a tired kid, and your own notes of it. Fine, he was heard before the zero. I'll want the version history and that page of Hamlet on paper, Hale, and you'll tell me what's on his record right now.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing tonight, and nothing on his record now or after. He'll do it to put this behind him, private, and marked before his December 1 deadline. The copies I asked for go in the same email, Hale.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday, after school. Who's in the room with him?
Do we have an agreement?
When it's in my inbox tonight, we do. And you still haven't said who's supervising him.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require copies of the version history and the page of Hamlet you showed me, and the name of the person who will supervise him. I expect all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, with the mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight, wants copies of what you showed her, and wants to know who will supervise him; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You opened the play to the scene and had her look for a line that isn't in it, because that was something she could check with her own eyes instead of taking your word.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it conclusive, which handed her the argument she came prepared to win.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing between 11:31 PM and midnight the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: In your first line, skip the checker entirely and start by owning the zero going in before you called, then go straight to the version history.
